clue.text: Content to leave Essex cabbie with pint in bar

indicators.note: the content of each word is its inside, so taking it away leaves just the first and last letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An Essex taxi driver is pictured drinking a pint at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content to leave' works on all three words: Essex gives EX, cabbie gives CE, pint gives PT. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, bar means leaving out or apart from, as in 'everyone bar me'.

clue.text: Language coming from artless earthlings

indicators.note: the language is made out of the letters left over, rearranged
the word art is removed, since 'artless' here reads as earthlings without art

explanation.surface: A language is said to be spoken by simple, unsophisticated humans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artless' reads as 'art less': take ART out of EARTHLINGS to leave EHLINGS, then rearrange those letters as 'coming from' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: English is the tongue of England and widely used around the world.

clue.text: Males in court case

indicators.note: the word for males is placed inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: hes, as in 'hes and shes', are males

explanation.surface: Men are involved in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'court case' as a lawsuit, but 'case' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest is a large box or trunk, a kind of case for storing things.

clue.text: Pair doctored photo of a Greek god

indicators.note: something doctored has been tampered with, so the letters of pair are rearranged

parts.note: pic is informal short for a picture or photo

explanation.surface: Two people faked a photograph of a deity from ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a Greek god' is a fair definition for an adjective: it means relating to Priapus.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Priapus, the Greek fertility deity famed for his permanent erection.

clue.text: Polish revolutionary moving to West as chubby-cheeked child

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so the revolutionary is shifted to the front

parts.note: to rub is to polish
Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A Polish rebel heads west, described as a child with chubby cheeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality, but it is the verb meaning rub. RUB then CHE, with CHE moved to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged infant angel in art, so the word is used for any plump, sweet-faced youngster.

clue.text: Scottish football team loves red suit

definitions.meaning: Heart of Midlothian, the Edinburgh club, known for short by this name
the verb as in 'I heart New York', meaning adores
one of the two red suits in a pack of playing cards, alongside diamonds

explanation.surface: A fan of a Scottish club is pictured loving their team's red kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate definitions of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an Edinburgh football club, means adores, and is a red card suit.

clue.text: Disconcert discounter discounting small discount

indicators.note: to disconcert is to throw into disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to discount is to leave out of account, so the letter for small is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A tongue-twister about upsetting a discount retailer by cutting a small discount.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from DISCOUNTER to leave DICOUNTER, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount is a cut in price, which is a reduction.

clue.text: Corbyn: "I struggle to be broodingly handsome"

indicators.note: letters that struggle are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: The Labour politician Jeremy Corbyn admits he finds it hard to look dark and dashing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CORBYN plus I. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the poet Lord Byron or his romantic heroes: moody, passionate and darkly attractive.

clue.text: Power outage, possible source of conflict

parts.note: power generation is the production of electricity, so generation stands for power
an outage is a break or interruption, a gap

explanation.surface: A power cut could cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Power outage' as one blackout; each word is read separately for its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The difference in attitudes between young people and their parents often leads to family disagreements.

clue.text: Regularly scrubbing toughened moulding

indicators.note: scrubbing every other letter of toughened in a regular pattern keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A decorative strip is cleaned often, having been hardened.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is an S-shaped curve used in architectural mouldings and arches.

clue.text: One reportedly defames northern folk

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the words are judged by how they come across in speech

parts.note: to defame someone is to slander them, so the word heard is slanders

explanation.surface: Someone is said to speak ill of others, as if gossip is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'I slanders' runs into a match for the people of the Arctic island nation; the split between the words shifts in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Iceland, just south of the Arctic Circle, are a northern nation.

clue.text: Reviewing cannabis? Mine is excellent

indicators.note: re-viewing taken as viewing backwards, so the two words are turned round together

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone tries some cannabis and declares their own stash superb.
explanation.walkthrough: POT then PIT, read backwards as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal word for first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Irresistible filling of tenth piece of cake

indicators.note: the filling is what lies inside, so the middle letters of tenth are taken

parts.note: icing is part of a cake, the sugary layer on top

explanation.surface: A tempting slice of cake has a delicious filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of TENTH is ENT; add ICING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing is so attractive and tempting that it is hard to resist.

clue.text: Achy shaking stopped by iodine, salt and kaolin

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are plugged in the middle by the other pieces
shaking jumbles the letters of achy into CHAY

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
NaCl, sodium chloride, is the chemical formula of common salt

explanation.surface: An aching patient is given iodine and salt, then kaolin, as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: ACHY shuffled gives CHAY; I and NACL go in to make CH-INACL-AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaolin is the fine white clay used to make porcelain, which is also known by this name.

clue.text: Complaint of writer about the British clearing banks

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for writer is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outside letters, and clearing them leaves only the inner part of the and British

explanation.surface: An author complains about the big British high-street banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing banks' looks like a banking term, but it strips the outer letters from THE (H) and BRITISH (RITIS). PEN reversed is NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, and this one is inflammation of the kidneys.

clue.text: Record in field event reduced by a third

indicators.note: the six-letter word loses a third of its letters, its last two

parts.note: the discus is an athletics field event

explanation.surface: A record set in a throwing event has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like an athletics record; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or other recording medium.

clue.text: Argument about bathroom fittings

indicators.note: about here signals turning the word round

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A couple quarrel over the choice of bathroom fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Taps on a basin or bath are among the fixtures fitted in a bathroom.

clue.text: Elitist rifle range welcoming dilettante

indicators.note: the phrase welcomes the answer in, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: A snobbish shooting club lets in an amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in things without seriousness, just like someone who trifles.

clue.text: It could be William Spooner's cherished reputation

indicators.note: William Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: nursed, as in nursed a hope, means cherished
fame is renown, a public reputation

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner's own name is pictured as something he treasured.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of 'nursed fame' to get the answer. 'William' doubles as Spooner's own given name.
explanation.definitionFit: William is an example of a forename, the personal name before a surname.

clue.text: English teacher and students getting up when day breaks

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up means read from bottom to top, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: An English teacher and his class rise at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: E, SIR and NUS are read upwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is dawn, the moment daylight first appears.

clue.text: Low walls of national interest illuminated by night

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle, moo

indicators.note: the walls are the outer letters, the first and last of national and of interest

explanation.surface: Low walls are pictured as being of national interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cow's call, not an adjective for walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by the moon, so bright at night.

clue.text: Accepted a good vibrator

parts.note: a reed vibrates to make the sound in a wind instrument

explanation.surface: A saucy picture: someone took delivery of a decent sex toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vibrator' plays on its saucy sense; it is the reed in a clarinet or oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed and accepted both mean consented to, as an offer or terms.

clue.text: Ridiculous ringtone is a gas!

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters of ringtone are absurdly jumbled

explanation.surface: A silly phone ringtone is hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' reads as 'great fun' in the surface; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a colourless chemical element that makes up most of the air.

clue.text: She doesn't appear to eat innards of fowl

parts.note: nosh is British slang meaning to eat

indicators.note: the innards are the inside, so the middle letters of fowl are taken

explanation.surface: A woman skips a meal of chicken guts and stays away.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a person who fails to turn up, such as a woman who doesn't arrive.

clue.text: Trail of droppings leads to shamefaced Rupert Bear

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the outer letters bear the droppings between them
the leads of words are their first letters, here those of shamefaced and Rupert

parts.note: poo is a childish word for droppings

explanation.surface: A trail of dung leads to a sheepish Rupert Bear, the cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rupert Bear' is a British children's comic-strip bear, but 'Bear' is a separate instruction. S and R hold POO.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or trail left by an animal, including its droppings.

clue.text: Celebrities dropping litter at Ickworth House

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the phrase holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: Famous people are scattering rubbish at Ickworth House, a National Trust stately home in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ickworth House' looks like one name; 'House' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The glitterati are fashionable, glamorous celebrities.

clue.text: Obsequious Oscar is sly when abandoning ship

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the letters for ship are taken away from is sly

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A cunning man named Oscar slips away from a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both S's from IS SLY to leave ILY.
explanation.definitionFit: An oily person is smarmy and ingratiating, unpleasantly eager to please.

clue.text: Live on border

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone lives on a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live or dwell there.

clue.text: Animal rights dividing supporters

indicators.note: the rights split the supporters apart by going between their letters

parts.note: feet support the body
R is the abbreviation for right, so two rights are RR

explanation.surface: An animal-rights issue causes a split among its campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: The ferret is a small domesticated polecat used for hunting rabbits.
